extracted.intended_audience: U.S. public company registrants, auditors, investors, and securities lawyers/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and commenter feedback on proposed and final SEC requirements for disclosing climate-related impacts on financial statements, including proposed Financial Impact Metrics and adopted narrower Expenditure Metrics. Focuses on thresholds, attribution, aggregation, definitions, and feasible disclosure formats for registrants' SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregated (separately stated) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disaggregated, or separately stated, disclosure of climate-related impacts on financial statement line items (analogous to segment reporting and other disaggregated disclosures under U.S. GAAP and IFRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites FASB ASC Topic 606, IFRS 15, and Article 5 of Regulation S-X as precedents; proposed requirement would disclose impacts of identified physical and transition risks on any financial statement metric. Commenters both supported greater granularity for investor decision-usefulness and raised concerns about operational burden and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Financial Impact Metrics (line-item impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that registrants disclose the impacts of any climate-related risks (physical and transition) on their financial statement metrics, on a line-item basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporters said investors would use these for investing, voting, engagement; opponents said companies don't currently track by line item, would need new systems, controls, and that disclosures could be non-comparable, costly, or inconsistent with GAAP. Commission ultimately did not adopt these proposed metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-percent numeric disclosure threshold (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a one percent threshold on a financial statement line-item basis to determine whether disclosure of climate-related impacts is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted benefits (bright-line, reduces underreporting) and concerns (too low, immaterial detail, inconsistent across registrants, auditability). Alternatives proposed included higher percentages (5% or 10%), line-item-dependent thresholds, thresholds anchored to total assets or income, dollar thresholds, or combining numerical and materiality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of climate-related financial impacts only when those impacts are material (rather than a fixed numeric threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued materiality aligns with how registrants track impacts internally, reduces operational burden, and better balances investor benefit vs cost. Some opposed, saying materiality could cause underreporting; some suggested materiality plus a backstop numeric threshold (e.g., 5% short-/medium-term or 10% long-term) or a dollar floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation method for determining threshold (absolute aggregation vs netting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to aggregate the absolute values of positive and negative impacts on a line-by-line basis before testing a disclosure threshold, use net values, or allow registrants to net against insurance recoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters disagreed: aggregating absolute values departs from typical accounting and may disclose individually immaterial items; netting may mask economic significance. Example guidance: disclose losses net of insurance when recovery probable and recognized in same period per FASB ASC 450-20. Some supported absolute aggregation as reflecting significance; others worried about greenwashing if netting used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow registrant-set minimum materiality thresholds for aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting registrants to set a minimum materiality threshold for individual items when applying any aggregation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested by commenters as a way to avoid disclosing individually immaterial items when aggregating absolute values; no specific method prescribed—commenters proposed flexibility to set reasonable cutoffs and disclose assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reporting for physical events vs transition activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Require registrants to determine disclosure thresholds and report impacts separately for physical (severe weather and other natural conditions) events and transition activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters supported separate reporting as consistent with TCFD; others argued the distinction may be unclear and recommended allowing aggregate disclosure. Commission considered these views when refining Expenditure Metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and terminology for 'severe weather events and other natural conditions'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and define 'severe weather events and other natural conditions' (term appeared variably as 'severe' vs 'extreme' in proposals) and provide examples or a definitional list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked for clarity on scope, whether to use a prescriptive list (some suggested third-party lists or a maintained list), how to assess severity (meteorological measures vs financial impact), regional differences in severity, event start/end dates, and whether events must be attributable to climate change or exceed historical baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'transition activities'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what constitutes transition activities, including whether ordinary efficiency efforts qualify and whether disclosure would force competitively sensitive information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters sought guidance on when a transition activity ends, whether to include activities by unrelated third parties that nonetheless affect the registrant, and sector-specific examples. Some suggested limiting required disclosures to specified transition activities (e.g., actions to reduce GHG emissions) or tying disclosure to management-identified transition items in Regulation S-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of effects to climate-related causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Require registrants to attribute financial impacts to climate-related events, conditions, or transition activities and provide rules or guidance on how to isolate or attribute effects when multiple contributing causes exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted many costs have mixed purposes and causes (e.g., insurance cost increases, mitigation investments). Suggested approaches include: attribute only when climate risk is a 'significant contributing factor' or when impacts are primarily/entirely driven by climate matters, permit reasonable estimates with disclosed assumptions, allow ranges, or provide qualitative explanations when disaggregation is infeasible. Some recommended requiring disclosure only when impacts are material and reasonably estimable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification guidance and allowance for estimates and ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow registrants to make reasonable estimates of climate impacts, and permit disclosure of either a single amount or a range, accompanied by disclosed assumptions and contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested explicit permission to estimate and to disclose assumptions so investors can interpret uncertainty; one commenter recommended allowing ranges with context, and others recommended guidance on how to determine single amounts if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow qualitative disclosures when disaggregation impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit registrants to explain qualitatively that required disaggregated information cannot be provided due to mixed causes or infeasibility, instead of forcing numerical attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested that when events have multiple contributing factors or attribution is impracticable, registrants should be allowed to provide qualitative context to avoid misleading or speculative numeric allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit disclosure to first-order/direct effects (alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit climate-impact disclosure to first-order or direct costs and impacts that can be readily identified and segregated in current financial records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters proposed focusing on direct, discrete expenditures (e.g., property damage, repair costs) because such items are straightforward to extract from current systems and audit. This approach reduces burden compared with attempting to capture indirect, supply-chain, or longer-term effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to GAAP-recognized impacts (alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict required climate-impact disclosures to those impacts that would be recognized under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended aligning disclosure obligations with GAAP recognition to avoid requiring information beyond the scope of existing accounting standards; this would exclude some proposed disclosure elements that lack GAAP treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete expenditures table format (alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a tabular note presenting discrete and separable expenditures (expensed and capitalized) in distinct categories: (i) climate-related events, (ii) transition activities for publicly disclosed climate targets/goals, and (iii) all other transition activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued discrete expenditures could be produced and audited with certainty consistent with GAAP financial statements; examples include a note to financial statements listing identifiable direct costs and capital expenditures incurred for the express purpose of addressing climate events and transition issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregated-category disclosure alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow aggregated disclosure by broad accounting categories (e.g., revenues, expenditures, profits; assets, liabilities, equity) instead of detailed line-item disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested to ensure investors can see magnitude without excessive complication; commenter recommended grouping costs/benefits into these simple buckets for comparability and reduced burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event/activity-level disclosure (alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report impacts at the event or activity level (discrete material climate events and transition activities) rather than on a per financial-statement-line-item basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested focusing on discrete, material events and activities to provide useful investor information while avoiding the operational burden of line-item mapping across the ledger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum required set of line items to enhance comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission could identify a minimum set of financial-statement line items for which climate-impact disclosure is required, allowing registrants to include additional line items as appropriate to their business model and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach aims to balance comparability across registrants with flexibility to reflect industry-specific financial statement presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-down approach linking Regulation S-K risk disclosures to financial impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a top-down linkage from short-term climate risks identified under Regulation S-K to required financial-statement impacts at a specified threshold, supplemented by other material impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One commenter recommended linking qualitative risk identification to quantitative financial impacts for the most significant short-term risks, reducing the need to track every transaction while ensuring material impacts are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate-related cash-flow metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose climate-related cash-flow metrics focused on gross cash flows of climate-related expenditures, with indication of which cash flows have been capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenter argued cash-flow metrics could provide a clearer picture of real cash impacts and could be directly linked to Regulation S-K disclosures; guidance would need to define gross vs net cash flows and capitalization treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific guidance for industries with prominent transition spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sector- or industry-specific guidance where registrants' balance sheets commonly reflect expenditures related to clean energy, decarbonization, or resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested tailored guidance would help companies in affected industries determine what constitutes transition-related expenses and improve consistency and comparability across registrants in the same sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditability and accounting-principles concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether accounting principles and auditing guidance exist for proposed disclosures and whether auditors can opine on required climate-impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised that lack of GAAP or auditing guidance for certain proposed metrics would hinder auditability; concerns included difficulty auditing future or unrealized impacts and private counterparty data collection, potentially requiring new standards or auditor procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational feasibility and cost/burden considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider registrants' current systems, processes, controls, and the costs of implementing tracking, quantification, and disclosure of climate impacts by line item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters stated registrants do not currently track impacts by line item, that implementing such tracking would be burdensome and costly, and that requirements should be tailored to what issuers can reasonably produce. The Commission cited these concerns in declining to adopt the proposed Financial Impact Metrics and instead adopting narrower Expenditure Metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure Metrics (final requirement adopted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of a discrete set of actual expenses that registrants incur and can attribute to severe weather events and other natural conditions (narrower than the proposed Financial Impact Metrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission adopted Expenditure Metrics after considering commenter concerns about burden and cost; these are intended to be feasible under current financial reporting processes and overlap with required disclosures of capitalized costs, expensed expenditures, charges, and losses under the final rules. Registrants remain obligated under GAAP to consider and disclose material impacts even if climate-driven.
